reasoning: kokkos.cpp:295-310: `Kokkos::InitializationSettings args;` is default-constructed and then immediately tested with `if (args.has_num_threads())`.  lib/kokkos/core/src/impl/Kokkos_InitializationSettings.hpp:15-28 defines the accessors via KOKKOS_IMPL_DECLARE over `std::optional<TYPE> m_##NAME;` with `bool has_##NAME() const noexcept { return static_cast<bool>(m_##NAME); }`, so a freshly constructed InitializationSettings has every optional disengaged and has_num_threads() is unconditionally false.  The 'Kokkos package already initalized. Cannot change parameters' warning is therefore unreachable, and with it the `nthreads = args.get_num_threads(); device = args.get_device_id(); ngpus = init_ngpus;` restore.  The static `init_ngpus` (declared kokkos.h:79, written at :309) is consequently write-only dead state.  The intended predicate is clearly `Kokkos::is_initialized()`, which is what KokkosLMP::initialize() at :494-501 actually uses to decide whether to call Kokkos::initialize(args).  Consequence: a second LAMMPS instance in the same process silently keeps the newly requested (but ineffective) nthreads/device/ngpus with no warning.
fix: Replace `if (args.has_num_threads())` with `if (Kokkos::is_initialized())` (keeping the same body), so the warning and the restore of nthreads/device/init_ngpus actually fire on a second instantiation.  Note get_num_threads()/get_device_id() must then be read from the live Kokkos state rather than from the empty `args`, e.g. keep static copies alongside init_ngpus.

reasoning: ComputeHexOrderAtomKokkos::operator()(TagComputeHexOrderAtom,ii) ends with `d_qnarray(i,0) = usum/nnn; d_qnarray(i,1) = vsum/nnn;` (compute_hexorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:189-190) and guards only with `if (ncount < nnn) { d_qnarray(i,0) = d_qnarray(i,1) = 0.0; return; }` (:161-164). For nnn > 0 the two agree, because `if (nnn > 0) { select2(...); ncount = nnn; }` on both sides makes ncount == nnn. Both are wrong on every atom, whereas the CPU style averages over all neighbours inside the cutoff (and returns 0 when there are none).

reasoning: The mechanism checks out on both sides.  (1) The shared-flags claim is real: lib/kokkos/containers/src/Kokkos_DualView.hpp:287-292 defines the subview constructor as `DualView(const DualView<DT,DP...>& src, const Arg0& arg0, Args... args) : modified_flags(src.modified_flags), d_view(subview(src.d_view,...)), h_view(subview(src.h_view,...))` -- the subview shares the parent's `modified_flags` View verbatim.  So `auto k_bondlist_m = Kokkos::subview(k_bondlist,m,Kokkos::ALL,Kokkos::ALL); k_bondlist_m.modify_device();` (bond_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:116-117) bumps the modified counter of the hybrid's own 3-D k_bondlist every step.  (2) bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp does its bond breaking on the HOST: :180 `neighborKK->k_bondlist.sync_host();`, :202 `h_bondlist(n,2) = 0;`, :249 `neighborKK->k_bondlist.modify_host();`.  Tracing one reneighbor interval: on step N the host zeros leave modified_host > modified_device; on step N+1 hybrid's `modify_device()` at :117 makes modified_device > modified_host, so quartic's `neighborKK->k_bondlist.sync<DeviceType>()` (bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp:112) copies nothing and the device row still holds the ORIGINAL nonzero bond type, and its `sync_host()` at :180 then copies device->host and wipes the zeros.  The device kernel's `if (bondlist(n,2) <= 0) return;` guard (bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp:266) therefore never fires for a bond broken earlier in the same interval.  ADJUSTMENTS: (a) The break is NOT lost permanently.  bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp:205-208 also sets `atom->bond_type[i1][m] = 0` (and the reverse), so at the next reneighbor Neighbor rebuilds the bondlist without that bond.  The real damage is confined to the rest of the current reneighbor interval: if the pair drifts back inside rc there, the quartic bond force and the pair correction are re-applied to a bond that the CPU version leaves broken.  (b) Reachability is narrower than stated.  BondHybrid::flags() (src/bond_hybrid.cpp:288-293) errors with 'Cannot hybridize bond styles with different topology settings' unless every sub-style has the same partial_flag, and quartic/kk is the only KOKKOS bond style with partial_flag == 1 (src/MOLECULE/bond_quartic.cpp:39; there is no BPM /kk bond style and bond_quartic_exp never sets it), while BondHybrid::settings() (:244-246) rejects the same style twice.  So the finding's example `bond_style hybrid/kk quartic/kk harmonic/kk` is refused at init; the only reachable configuration is a single-sub-style `bond_style hybrid/kk quartic/kk`.
fix: Do not call modify_device() on the shared-flag subview.  Give each sub-style bondlist its own modified_flags -- e.g. build k_bondlist_m from the device/host subviews with the two-View DualView constructor (`DAT::tdual_int_2d(Kokkos::subview(k_bondlist.view_device(),m,ALL,ALL), Kokkos::subview(k_bondlist.view_host(),m,ALL,ALL))`, which allocates fresh flags), keep it in a per-style array so the flags persist between steps, and mark it modified in the space the hybrid actually wrote (device, only on a reneighbor step).
